newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA LIMITS RUBBER PRICES MOVES TO CONTROL RISK.
newsitem.headline: CHINA LIMITS RUBBER PRICES MOVES TO CONTROL RISK.

text.p: The China Commodity Exchange will limit price movements in the key August 1997 rubber contract to within 40 yuan per day from Friday in an effort to bring some control to the market, the exchange in a statement on Thursday.
The current daily limit-up and limit-down levels for the contract is 400 yuan, traders said.
The exchange would also increase the margin requirement of the contract to 80 percent from Wednesday, August 13, the statement from the exchange in southern Hainan province said.
The exchange has already announced that the margin requirement was raised to 25 percent from August 4, and would be raised to 30 percent from August 11 for long positions.
The margin requirement was usually 6.5 percent, traders said.

The exchange has introduced a series of measures including banning investors from building new positions in the August contract and temporarily suspending trade to cool over-speculation, traders said.
The August contract has fluctuated in a wide range in recent weeks as the confrontation between longs and shorts has grown increasingly fierce.
The contract ended Thursday down 400 yuan at 11,300 ($1,361) per tonne in thin volume of 1,010 tonnes.
Delivery in the August contract begins on August 18.
